newsitem.title: GERMANY: RWE, Veba could easily find new partners - analysts.
newsitem.headline: RWE, Veba could easily find new partners - analysts.

text.p: German analysts said on Tuesday that it would not be difficult for German diversified utilities RWE and Veba to find another telecoms partner, as their alliance with C&W Plc looked in jeopardy.
"Veba and RWE will find another Anglo-Saxon partner. Germany is the biggest telephonic market in Europe," said Thomas Deser, utilities analyst at BHF Bank in Frankfurt.
"It is only a question of time. SBC is a possibility, BellSouth is a possibility -- it could be any of these, for example," said Deser.

Peter Antes, utilities analyst at Bayerische Vereinsbank: "A cold winter is more important to the bottom line of these companies than any telecoms information. If it is true that Cable and Wireless have pulled out, then Veba and RWE could find another partner," said Antes.
"They could also decide to go without a partner. However, if C&W do pull out, this will delay their plans in the telecommunications area and it could make things more expensive," said Antes.
C&W formed a strategic alliance, called Vebacom, in 1995. Last year, the firms agreed to bring RWE into the deal and final contracts were drawn up two weeks ago.
C&W has not yet signed the deal and British newspapers have speculated it is poised to pull out of the German partnership to join a larger global alliance.
German sources said Veba had already offered C&W terms to leave the partnership. A spokeswoman for Veba said she could neither confirm nor deny any offer had been made.
